headline: Wilderness Permits and Central Cascade Access
reservation: Managed wilderness permits are required for specific trailheads in the Central Cascades between June and October. These are separate from Forest Service parking passes or lodging bookings at popular spots like Elk Lake. Systems change annually; check the official U.S. Forest Service or Recreation.gov portals for the current season's entry requirements.

days.title: Rivers and Volcanic Landscapes
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Old Mill District

stops.name: Drake Park
stops.detail: Walk through this historic riverside park along Mirror Pond for a view of Bend's iconic downtown setting.

stops.name: Newberry National Volcanic Monument
stops.detail: Visit the Lava Lands Visitor Center to walk across the basalt flows of the Lava Butte cinder cone.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to reach the Lava Lands area; Paulina Lake requires an additional 30 minutes south.
days.note: Newberry access involves multiple distant sites; select one primary area to avoid excessive driving.

days.title: High Desert Rims and River Paths

stops.name: Smith Rock State Park
stops.detail: View the towering rhyolite cliffs and watch climbers on the Monkey Face formation from the rim trails.

stops.name: Deschutes River Trail
stops.detail: Follow the riverside paths south of town for views of Benham Falls and basalt rock outcrops.

days.driving: Allow 60 minutes between Smith Rock and southern river trailheads; conditions vary with highway traffic.
days.note: Smith Rock parking often reaches capacity by mid-morning during the sunny season.

days.title: Cascade Lakes Scenic Route

stops.name: Mount Bachelor
stops.detail: Take the scenic chairlift for a panoramic view of the Three Sisters and the surrounding high desert.

stops.name: Elk Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy a shoreline picnic or non-motorized paddle with a direct view of South Sister's volcanic peak.

days.driving: Allow 90 minutes for a round trip along the Scenic Byway; high elevation means slower travel.
days.note: The Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway is closed seasonally by snow; check ODOT reports for opening dates.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Parking at popular spots like Devil's Lake or Smith Rock fills before 9 AM on summer weekends. Use the Mount Bachelor shuttle during peak season if available to reach high-elevation trailheads.

intel.title: High Elevation Gaps
intel.text: Cellular coverage drops off once you pass the Seventh Mountain area on the way to the lakes. Carry paper maps for any navigation beyond the Bend city limits.

intel.title: Last Gas Warnings
intel.text: Fuel is plentiful in Bend and Redmond, but there are no service stations along the Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway. Ensure a full tank before departing for remote volcanic sites south of Sunriver.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Openings
intel.text: Higher elevation roads, including the path to Paulina Peak, typically do not open until June or July. Wildfire smoke can impact visibility and health in late summer; check AQI data daily.

intel.title: Waterway Requirements
intel.text: Oregon requires an Invasive Species Permit for non-motorized boats 10 feet or longer. Life jackets are mandatory for all paddlers on the Deschutes River and Cascade Lakes.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at RDM airport, stock up on water and sun protection in Redmond, then drive 25 minutes to Bend lodging.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for unpaved Forest Service roads; standard sedans are fine for the Scenic Byway.
plan.goldenHour: Pilot Butte offers a 360-degree sunset view over the Cascade Range, though the summit road has specific seasonal hours.
